bounded_predicate: A per-file visitor collects private KtClass declarations, then simple class-like names from calls, type references, annotations, callable/class references and qualified receivers plus import prefixes. Any same-name entry can retain a private class without symbol resolution. Entity.from(the entire private class). No rule-specific options.
selection_rationale: Adds bounded private class retention/removal advice, not another visibility policy rule. The three extra cases distinguish type-use, scoped-name ambiguity and reflective legitimate use.

positive.intent: An unreferenced private helper is separate from public API policy and can confuse readers. The advisory is bounded to this file and its syntactic usage collector.

negative.intent: The private helper is actually named as a constructor callee; it remains useful and is not reported.

suppression.intent: Genuine file-scoped upstream suppression only on a package-isolated positive copy. The byte-identical unsuppressed Case.kt keeps all authored ranges; no host filtering or ktChecker-ID alias.

controls.intent: A private type used only in another private declaration signature is retained. This is a valid type-reference boundary, not proof that either declaration is reachable.
Only the inner scoped LocalIndex is constructed, but the collector uses simple names and retains the unused outer private class too. Preserve the anticipated miss.

limitations: No rule-specific options exist; the lifecycle disabled case is not presented as a real detector option.
Reflection, serialization frameworks and generated/dynamic uses are not absence-of-use evidence. Same-name scope collisions and import-prefix heuristics can also miss genuinely unused declarations.
Private objects and global call-graph liveness are not the selected KtClass predicate.

Local syntactic advice only. No binding identity, safe automatic rewrite, whole-program reachability, binary ABI compatibility, call effect, reflection completeness, performance or semantic qualification follows.

The six lifecycle cases include a disabled-rule configuration control, pinned-version positive replay and negative child-snapshot replay; the latter two are not new predicates. Every other negative/control keeps this rule active.

Only the existing explicit JVM LIGHT input is proposed. Common and Native requests must abstain without launching; no parser/compiler/Kotlin 2.4.21 versus embedded 2.4.10 compatibility or multiplatform qualification.
File-level suppression is authored; declaration-level aliases, baselines and generated-code inclusion policy are not newly qualified.
